questions.q: In the diagnostic order this capstone recommends, what should you check first when a training job seems slower than expected?
options: Open Nsight Compute and profile every kernel in detail
Run nvidia-smi dmon to get a cheap, broad view of GPU utilization across all GPUs
Rewrite the model architecture
Immediately reinstall the NVIDIA driver
questions.explain: The diagnostic order goes from cheap and broad to expensive and detailed. nvidia-smi dmon costs nothing to run and can immediately rule out entire categories of problems, like a single straggler GPU.

questions.q: In the scenario, all 4 GPUs show low, even utilization (around 35%). What does this suggest?
options: One specific GPU is malfunctioning and needs replacement
Every GPU is likely spending significant time waiting on something upstream, rather than one GPU being a straggler
The GPUs are running at maximum efficiency
The CUDA Toolkit version is incompatible
questions.explain: Low, fairly even utilization across all GPUs rules out one misbehaving card (a straggler) and instead points toward a shared upstream bottleneck, such as data loading or communication, affecting all GPUs similarly.

questions.q: What does timing the gap between batches in the data loader help diagnose?
options: Whether the GPU's tensor cores are being used
Whether a CPU-bound data loader is starving the GPU between batches
Whether NVLink is connected correctly
Whether the model has enough parameters
questions.explain: A large gap between batches combined with low GPU utilization during that gap indicates the data loader (a CPU-side process) can't keep up, starving the GPU of work — a CPU-bound bottleneck, not a GPU-side one.

questions.q: Why would a team check the NCCL debug log (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO) as part of this diagnosis?
options: To check whether the all-reduce communication is still using NVLink or has silently fallen back to a slower transport
To verify the model's test accuracy
To check how much disk space is available
To confirm the Python version being used
questions.explain: The NCCL debug log shows which transport (like NVLink) was actually used for each communication channel, which can reveal a silent regression to a slower path — for example after a driver update or a change in GPU placement.

questions.q: Why does this diagnostic approach check data loading and communication before opening a detailed profiler like Nsight Compute?
options: Because Nsight Compute cannot run on multi-GPU jobs
Because cheaper, broader checks can rule out entire categories of problems quickly, saving the more expensive and detailed profiling step for last
Because Nsight Compute only works on CPUs
Because profiling a kernel always takes less time than checking nvidia-smi
questions.explain: The diagnostic discipline is to start broad and cheap, ruling out likely categories (straggler GPU, CPU-bound loader, communication regression) before reaching for the most expensive and detailed tool, which should only be needed once simpler explanations are eliminated.
